Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.
slides: Welcome back, and now the first kind of overlap question, the range. Here a fact is missing, so we can't find the exact overlap.

slides.say: Remember the pizza? We couldn't say exactly how many slices have both. We could only say the least, one, and the most, three.
So in a range question we look for two numbers. The biggest overlap that is possible. And the smallest overlap that must be, because there's no other choice.
at: The biggest overlap that is possible

slides.say: Let's see an example. There are fifteen students. Ten take art, and nine take drama. How many could take both?

slides: We don't know how many take neither, and we don't know how many take both. That's the missing fact. So the answer is a range.

slides.say: Let's draw the fifteen students as fifteen boxes. The ten shaded boxes are the art students.
First the smallest overlap. We want as few students in both as we can. So we give drama to the students without art first.
Five students don't take art, so five drama places go to them.
Nine minus five is four. So four drama places are left, and every student without art already takes drama.
So the last four have to go to art students. There's no other choice. So at least four students take both.
at: at least four students take both

slides.say: Now the biggest overlap. This time we want as many students in both as we can. So we give all nine drama places to art students.
Can it be more than nine? No, because only nine students take drama. So the overlap is somewhere from four to nine.
at: Can it be more than nine

slides.say: Now let's find these two numbers without drawing. The biggest overlap is the size of the smaller group.
at: The biggest overlap is the size

slides: Why? We put the whole small group inside the big group. So every drama student also takes art. And it can't be more, because the small group has no more members.

slides.say: Ten and nine, so the biggest overlap is nine. There's nothing to calculate.
Let's see it with other numbers. There are twenty students. Eight have a dog, and twelve have a cat. The biggest overlap is eight, the smaller group. All eight dog owners can also have a cat.
And if the groups are equal? Say six and six. Then the biggest overlap is six. The two groups can be the very same six people.
at: Then the biggest overlap is six

slides.say: When the two groups add up to more than the total, some overlap is forced. The smallest overlap is the sum of the two groups, minus the total. That is the extra count above the total.
at: The smallest overlap is the sum

slides.say: Ten plus nine is nineteen. But there are only fifteen students. Nineteen minus fifteen is four.
Why does this work? Think of nineteen places in art and drama, for only fifteen students. Even if every student gets one place, four places are left over.

slides: Those four places have to go to students who already have one. So four students must take both. It's the same four we found with the boxes.

slides.say: One more example. There are thirty players. Eighteen wear a cap, and twenty-one wear gloves. Eighteen plus twenty-one is thirty-nine. Thirty-nine minus thirty is nine. So at least nine wear both.
Now what if the two groups don't go over the total? Let's go back to the twenty students. Eight have a dog, and twelve have a cat.
Eight plus twelve is twenty, exactly the total. So we can give the dogs and the cats to different students. Nobody has to have both.
So the smallest overlap is zero.
at: So the smallest overlap is zero

slides.say: And if the sum is even smaller? Say only five have a dog. Five plus twelve is seventeen, less than twenty.
A lot of students take seventeen minus twenty, and get minus three. But an overlap can't be negative. Nothing goes over the total, so the smallest overlap is zero.
at: seventeen minus twenty, and get minus three
so the smallest overlap is zero

slides.say: So we always ask, how far do the groups go over the total? If they don't go over it, the smallest overlap is zero. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
at: If they don't go over it
